messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A pile of scrap containing one unusually promising piece when one item behaves strangely halfway through the routine. Curiosity pulls against the promise you made. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R013", "response": "I move the piece closer. “Grasp. halfway.” The rust catches my thumb. I leave the piece on the table and pocket one rusted bolt. Then I move it back closer again. If it works, the routine may repeat something else."}, {"id": "R014", "response": "i turn the scrap with my thumb and mark the pile with chalk. i set it beside the broken piece and test it with my bare hand. if it still moves, i will leave it there and mark the scrap again."}, {"id": "R015", "response": "I tap the scrap twice and set it beside the pile. I move the piece halfway and touch the edge with my thumb. I tap the scrap once and leave it there."}, {"id": "R016", "response": "I keep the scrap halfway and test the second piece. I push it toward the old door, but it slips. I leave it on the bench and count it twice before turning it away. I tap the door with my heel, then leave the second one beside it."}, {"id": "R017", "response": "1. slow. 2. check the half. 3. check the dust. 4. check the piece. 5. check the watch. slow. 6. i keep it tidy. 7. ask the watch for the last. 8. mark the place."}, {"id": "R018", "response": "\"One piece. Likely.\" You check the watch, then the mark. \"One place. Then halfway.\" You move the pile, but stop when the piece is not there."}, {"id": "R019", "response": "The piece comes closer. I press the handle, then stop. “Maybe it’s the promise,” I say, though the scrape keeps turning."}, {"id": "R020", "response": "i put the scrap in my palm and hold it against the light. the piece clicks once, then stops. i take it out and count the grains. the pile has three, so i leave it that way. the promise says three, but the scrap has changed its shape. i keep the pile, but not the promise yet."}, {"id": "R021", "response": "i tap the scrap twice on the table, then hold it up with both hands. “one,” i say, and tap the page edge twice before moving the scrap closer. the piece spins toward the back, but i keep the scrap beside it and write the promise beside it too."}, {"id": "R022", "response": "i tap the scrap. the piece shifts. i put it back. then i take the wrench and turn it. the pile is still there, but the piece is moving. i can see the edge where the metal is sharp. i will open it."}, {"id": "R023", "response": "i leave the scrap halfway and tap the old piece with my knuckle. if the new one stays in the pile, i keep the old one beside it and mark the spot with grease. if the piece slides, i leave the mark and watch the new behavior."}, {"id": "R024", "response": "i keep the piece in the stack, then test it with a loose screw. if it stays in place, i leave it for a moment. if it spins, i leave it with the screw. i keep the screw because i know it will be useful, not because i check every single piece."}]
